[engine] If a difference reproduces with the SAME structure at two DISJOINT slices of the axis you suspected, that axis is not the variable -- stop deepening it and look for a property of the container instead. Two windows that agree on 'which items differ' rather than 'the first item that differs' have already answered the question.

<!-- lesson_id: eng-diag-0019 | class: diagnosis | superseded_by: - -->

**class**: `diagnosis`

## 為什麼（because）

The S1 divergence had been chased through the layer axis: the decode capture reported 480/480 layers differing, including layer 0, so the natural next move was to walk deeper layer windows to find the first bad layer. That ladder was uninterpretable from the start -- decode step 0's layer-0 input descends from the prefill's KV and the two arms' prefills already disagree (M1 5/9), so every decode layer is downstream of an earlier divergence, and there is no 'identical input' origin at which a first divergence can be defined. Re-running it where the input IS identical by construction (prefill, layer 0 = embedding) produced the answer: probing layers 0-3 and then layers 4-7 (disjoint, 8 layers, 6 graphs, 2 arms = 96 pairings) returned the SAME structure both times. Crucially the two rungs did not agree on which layer first diverges -- they agreed that divergence tracks a property of the GRAPH, not of the layer: slab-served graphs (256/256 experts resident) were bit-identical across all 8 probed layers, pool-served graphs (143/256) diverged from the first pooled layer on. The predictor was verified against an independent runtime marker, `CGC-PREFILL-STREAM: il=0 kind=0 ntok=182`, which appears on exactly the two all-EQ graphs. The cost of the misdirection was real: the first capture attempt pinned all 40 layers in every graph and killed the process at load (see eng-mh-0012), and two layer windows were measured before the orthogonal property was noticed.

## 反例（counterexample_observed）

A layer ladder measured twice, 0-3 and 4-7, whose two windows agreed on the divergence structure rather than on a first-divergent index -- the signature that the layer index was never the variable, while the analysis was still framed as 'find the first bad layer'.
